### Ô Môn Complex (Cần Thơ)
The Ô Môn power center is designed for four plants totaling ~3,810 MW.

citations.cited_text: Cụ thể như sau: Nhà máy nhiệt điện Ô Môn 1 do tập đoàn điện lực Việt Nam làm chủ đầu tư. Công suất của nhà máy này là 660MW, nhà máy này đã được đưa v...
citations.title: Danh sách nhà máy nhiệt điện ở miền Nam - Công ty TNHH TM-DV Vi Tính Thịnh Tâm

content.text: Ô Môn I (660 MW) is operating, owned by EVN.

Ô Môn II, III, and IV (~1,050 MW each) are planned to use gas from the Lô B offshore field (Block B – Ô Môn gas pipeline), which itself has been delayed for over a decade. The Ô Môn gas-to-power chain is classified as a national priority project under Decision 270/QĐ-TTg.

### Sơn Mỹ LNG (Bình Thuận)
Two planned LNG-to-power plants (Sơn Mỹ I and Sơn Mỹ II, each ~2,250 MW) are linked to the Sơn Mỹ LNG terminal.

citations.cited_text: The Revised PDP8 specifically requires the LNG Ca Na Project, LNG Quynh Lap, LNG Nghi Son, LNG Long Son, LNG Bac Lieu and LNG Son My I&II projects...
citations.title: Vietnam makes major updates to Power Development Plan VIII - Watson Farley & Williams

content.text: The Revised PDP8 specifically requires the Sơn Mỹ I&II projects to ensure operational progress.

Investors include AES (Sơn Mỹ II) and a consortium for Sơn Mỹ I. Terminal development is critical-path. **Confidence: LOW** — no financial close, no construction start.

### Nhơn Trạch 3&4 (Đồng Nai)
Vietnam's first LNG-fired CCGT plants, developed by PV Power. Combined capacity ~1,624 MW (2×812 MW). Linked to the Thị Vải LNG terminal. Entered commercial operation in 2024–2025. **Confidence: HIGH** — multiple government and operator confirmations.
